page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.2xlarge is an ARM-based general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors operating at 3.3 GHz, the server delivers 8 physical cores supporting 8 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core. The system includes 32.0 GB of memory, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided through a bundled 474 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by a 4 Gbps baseline network throughput. There are no discrete GPUs configured on this instance type.

Benchmark results highlight notable strengths in memory throughput and compression pipelines. In PassMark memory testing, the instance scored 4334.73, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded data handling is equally strong, with gzip compression reaching 36.56 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 17.53 GB/sec. For lightweight artificial intelligence tasks, the server records top-tier generation rates of 393.87 tokens per second on small 135M models. In contrast, PassMark cryptographic testing placed in the lower 25% bracket at 2358.83, and medium 7B model prompt processing registered in the bottom quartile at 22.61 tokens per second. Standard multi-core stress testing, web serving throughput of 29.3 GB/sec, and Redis operations at 25.37 million operations per second align with median platform averages.

The presence of high-speed local NVMe storage and dedicated ARM cores provides favorable resource density for throughput-bound operations without multithreading contention. The architecture avoids virtualization overhead, though it lacks x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX-512. The m9gd.2xlarge is structurally suited for static web hosting, Redis in-memory caching tiers, microservices, local logging nodes, and databases requiring low-latency scratch storage.

The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Bundled with 474 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, it operates without discrete GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, the instance achieves top-tier results in PassMark memory testing and single-threaded compression throughput, though cryptographic instruction tests and 7B model prompt processing perform in the lower quartiles. General computing, web serving throughput, and Redis operations register consistently within median ranges. The m9gd.2xlarge is effectively engineered for high-throughput microservices, caching infrastructure, data compression pipelines, and transactional database workloads that benefit from direct local NVMe instance storage.
